## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5fe2149385301e15afcde5fe15d33f4d6434ff49`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md, .github/workflows/release.yml + scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run-card.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs, docs/releases-maintenance.md, scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs (main, untouched), scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh (main, untouched), .github/workflows/scheduled-full-run-card.yml (main, untouched), AGENTS.md Prime Directive 15 (main, untouched)

Read against: PR #30862 head `5fe2149385` (7 files, +2347/-177, merge base `26c965cb8f`), fetched read-only into `refs/review/pr-30862`; card #30832 body and all four comments (6678236253, claim 6678280375, dev reports 6679395057 and 6685251006 — read as claims); rulings #29466 6663894403 and 6677910954; the maintainer's five confirmed landing details of 2026-11-06 11:32Z, verbatim as agreed. The dev reports' conclusions were not inputs to the verdict; every claim below was checked in the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

**The safety line — holds.**

- A `schedule` event cannot publish. The only job with a publish command on either cron is `snapshot-next` (release.yml 2523–2732), held whole at `environment: release`, needing `snapshot-next-preflight` with `success() && needs.snapshot-next-preflight.outputs.refusal == '' && (cron '17 1 * * *' || snapshot dispatch)`. The stable `publish` (1723–1727) needs `release-integrity` + `full-battery` under `success()`; `release-integrity` (1065–1067) and `stale-prompts` (1565–1567) run on `push` or a non-refresh dispatch only; `full-battery` needs `release-integrity`; `docker` (2212) gates on two outputs that are unset on a schedule; `version-pr` (224–226) now names its own cron `'0 */6 * * *'` — strictly subtractive against main, where it ran on any `schedule`. No stable job's `if:` was widened; the stable lane's diff is the `version-pr` conjunct alone.
- A stable dispatch or push cannot start a snapshot job: all four snapshot jobs' `if:` carry the same two arms (the daily cron, or `workflow_dispatch && inputs.snapshot_next && !inputs.refresh_version_pr`); `push` satisfies neither; the fleet-write reader (`validate.mjs` `jobsStartedBy`, now cron-aware) pins push → no snapshot job, bookkeeping cron → `version-pr` alone, repair/force/refresh dispatch → no snapshot job, snapshot dispatch → preflight alone with the three dependants `mayRun`.
- The supersede (`snapshot-next.mjs` `judgeSnapshotPrompts`, 1244–1290) cancels only a run that is: not the calling run, holding no job matching `PUBLISH_JOB_NAME`, `event === 'schedule'`, run status `waiting`, with a `Snapshot next of main SHA12 (awaiting approval)` job `waiting`, pending on environment `release`, and created before the calling run — in that order, each other case `untouched` with its reason. The job runs on the daily cron alone (2768–2771), never on a dispatch, needs the preflight alone, holds `actions: write` + `contents: read`, and skips on a quiet skip (`refusal == ''` conjunct) so yesterday's prompt stands when today proposes nothing. `cancel-in-progress` stays `false` on `release-snapshot-next-REF`. A transient read failure defers (exit 0, warning, no POST); any other read failure or a non-202/409 cancel answer is red.
- `stable-lane` reads through a client constructed with `dryRun: true`, which throws on every non-GET before `fetch` — structural, not a flag. `stale-prompts` and `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs` are byte-identical to main (diff empty).
- PD15: `AGENTS.md` is not in the diff (0 changed lines). The snapshot job's `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, one call of `scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh` (unchanged, one `changeset publish --tag next --no-git-tag`), no tag push, no Release, no dist-tag write — all re-pinned by `snapshotWiring`.

**The five confirmed details, in the tree.**

1. 时间 — `- cron: '17 1 * * *'` (release.yml 274), named identically in the four snapshot jobs' `if:`; `DAILY_CRON` pin refuses anything but one `M H * * *` tick; the hour is argued at 243–273 from measured nightly finishes. Holds.
2. 旧提示替换 — as above: an older schedule-started run still waiting at `release` is cancelled once today's preflight passed with no refusal; a human dispatch is never cancelled (`run.event !== 'schedule'` → untouched, pinned). Holds.
3. 静默跳过 — on `schedule` each of the five kinds concludes exit 0 with `refusal=KIND` + `reason=` recorded, a `::notice::` and a summary section; later preflight steps are gated `steps.X.outputs.refusal == ''`, `snapshot-next` and `snapshot-next-supersede` require the job output empty, the card job requires the preflight `failure`. Traced: (a) `same-commit` and (b) `rc-cycle` and (c) `debut` through `preflight --commit … --quiet-skip` → `proposalVerdict` `skipped`; (e) `stable-lane --quiet-skip` the same way; (d) `no-green-commit` in the select step's shell (2415–2429) on `--snapshot-commit` exit 1 with `.ok == false and .commit == null` (`runSnapshotCommit` emits exactly that record on "no commit qualifies", and a different record + exit 3 on NOT MEASURED). The switch is one expression, `QUIET_SKIP_EXPRESSION`, on the three refusing calls plus the select step's `EVENT_NAME` test; the post-approval preflight carries no `--quiet-skip` (pinned). NOT MEASURED stays loud on either start: `proposalVerdict` returns exit 3 with `reason` alone whenever anything is unread, even beside an expected refusal (then exit 1, `reason` alone); the select step re-exits with status 3. **A human dispatch refuses loudly for four of the five kinds — and for the fifth it files a card it must not: see must-fix 1.**
4. 通知 — `snapshot-next-card` (2832–2899): `needs: [snapshot-next-preflight, snapshot-next]`, `always() && ARMS && ((preflight failure && refusal == '') || snapshot failure)`, `permissions: contents: read, issues: write`, no `actions:`; one `actions/github-script` step importing `snapshotCardStep` from `scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run-card.mjs`, which re-judges the case from the same five env keys and calls the full-run card's own `fileOrRefreshCard` with the same callbacks (`cardCallbacks`, now shared by both steps — no second filer). Identity: fixed title `next snapshot lane: unexpected refusal or publish failure`, plain-text marker `os-next-snapshot-lane-card`, labels `bug`, `domain:devx`, `priority:p1` on create only, own footer. The publish-failure body says a partial publish is fixed by a fresh complete snapshot with a new timestamp, never a republish into it, never a touch of `latest`; it names the reason, run link, candidate commit and the version reached (or "nothing reached npm"). Success and quiet skips file nothing at both the job `if:` and the step. Holds, except as the must-fix says.
5. 要改的文本 — one new `## Amendment (2026-11-06, #30832)` section plus dated pointer callouts in the house shape under D1, D4, D5, 2026-11-05 bound line 2, the "Dispatch-only, and exclusive" requirement, the ⛔ list and "Not decided here"; the Status line gains one `· **Amended** (2026-11-06 …)` clause. D1–D6's decision text, the 2026-09-29 amendment and the 2026-11-05 bound lines are otherwise byte-unchanged in the diff. The amendment states "no `schedule` can publish" (line 310 and 267), "⛔ Prime Directive #15 is unchanged", "Option B … was not chosen". No `UNCONFIRMED`, `landing detail N of 5` or "being confirmed" text remains anywhere in the seven files. Holds, with two text should-fixes below.

**The two readings the dev took (③ of the brief).**

- The card also filing when the snapshot job fails after the approval but before the publish: inside detail 4 — the maintainer approved a publish that then did not happen; the body says "the version step did not run: nothing reached npm" (`renderSnapshotCardBody`, pinned). Silence there would leave an approved failure unreported, which detail 4 exists to prevent. Not a decision beyond the list.
- A `next` snapshot on npm recording no `gitHead` read as an unexpected refusal (`same-commit-unrecorded`), not a pass-through: detail 3's "没有新提交" is defined by the recorded commit, so an unreadable record cannot satisfy it; PD15 names an unordered publish an incident. A mechanism reading the list left to the lane, consistent with it and stated in the PR body and the script header; not a reversal of anything confirmed. Acceptable.

**The new pieces (④ of the brief).**

- `record-commit` writes `gitHead: COMMIT` into every publishable `package.json` after the version step (never committed); `guard --commit` reads it back from every PACKED manifest (`packedManifestProblems`, refuses a missing or other `gitHead`); the job's checkout is the selected commit, so npm's own HEAD-derived `gitHead` would equal it too; `readPublishedCommit` GETs the anchor (`@objectstack/cli`) version document at `REGISTRY/name/version` and reads top-level `gitHead` (40-hex or null), refusing a document for another version or a non-200 as unreadable. Written and read back the same way.
- `readStableLane` calls `collectWaitingRuns` (the waiting filter PLUS each version commit's push run by `head_sha`) and `collectPublishRuns` (`in_progress` + `queued` + the version-commit push run), merged by id, judged with `PUBLISH_JOB_NAME` / `PUBLISH_SETTLED_JOB_STATUSES` — the stable sweep's own readers and constants, imported, not copied. An in-flight run whose jobs are `null` is `unread` (NOT MEASURED). Note: `collectWaitingRuns` leaves `jobs: []` (not `null`) on a run it listed but did not read past its status; such a run is judged clear unless `collectPublishRuns` also saw it — covered today because every in-flight run is in the in-flight filters or the version-commit push, and `collectPublishRuns` throws when a filter's `total_count` exceeds its listing.
- Card permissions minimal; the arms keep it off push, the bookkeeping cron and every non-snapshot dispatch (pinned by `jobsStartedBy`).
- Step-output gating traced end to end: a failure writes `reason` only and exits non-zero → job red → `snapshot-next` skipped (`success()`), supersede skipped, card files; a quiet skip writes `refusal` + `reason`, exits 0 → later steps skipped by their `if:`, job green, `snapshot-next`/supersede skipped by the `refusal == ''` conjunct, card skipped (`result == 'success'`). Neither is mistaken for the other. Exit 3 is never converted to 0 (`proposalVerdict`, the select step's `exit "$status"`, the CLI's catch blocks).

**Pins and self-tests (⑤).** Read, not run: `snapshotWiring` gains the clock pins (`declaredCrons`, `guardClock`: two crons, each named by exactly one scheduled job and no `!=`), the supersede job's shape, the `refusal`/`reason` output chains over the four refusing steps, the `QUIET_SKIP_EXPRESSION` on every refusing call and nowhere bare, no `quiet-skip` after the approval, `stable-lane` exactly once and never after the approval, `--commit` on both preflights, `record-commit` between version and guard, `guard --commit`, the `refusal == ''` conjunct on `snapshot-next` and the supersede, and the card job's presence, `always()`, two cases, needs, permissions, step module/step, five env keys and arms. Each firing case in the batteries "two clocks" (13), "the daily supersede job" (9), "the quiet skip and the card" (16) and "the snapshot wiring" (21) mutates the checked-in text at the named site and asserts the named finding substring; I confirmed each regex matches the head text it means to mutate (indentation and spelling). `validate.mjs` `jobsStartedBy` gains `schedule` and answers UNKNOWN when the cron is not named — the "does not guess which clock" control pins it. The gate-carrying check-runs that execute these self-tests on the head (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`) are `success`. One pin gap is what lets must-fix 1 through: the `refusal=no-green-commit` pin tests presence of the string in the job, not the dispatch branch.

**Must-fix**

1. **The select step misclassifies a human dispatch's `no-green-commit` refusal as unexpected, and the card files for it.** release.yml 2430–2432: on a dispatch with `.commit == null` the step writes `reason=…` only — no `refusal=no-green-commit` — and exits 1. `snapshot-next-card`'s first case is `needs.snapshot-next-preflight.result == 'failure' && needs.snapshot-next-preflight.outputs.refusal == ''`, and `snapshotCardCase` judges the same inputs the same way, so a maintainer who dispatches `snapshot_next` while `main` has no fully green commit gets a `priority:p1` `bug` card whose body says "The preflight refused for a reason that is none of the five expected ones" while its reason line says main has no green commit. This contradicts the ADR text landed in this PR (line 293–294: an expected refusal on a dispatch is a loud red run; "a quiet skip files nothing" and the card's two cases are an UNEXPECTED refusal or a publish failure), the lane header ("a DISPATCH keeps today's loud refusal … no card"), `scheduled-full-run.mjs`'s card comment ("files NOTHING either way") and the PR body ("the same reading on a dispatch exits 1 with the same outputs"). The four script-driven kinds get it right because `proposalVerdict`'s `refused-expected` records `refusal` on exit 1; the shell branch does not. Fix: write `refusal=no-green-commit` on the dispatch branch too, and give `snapshotWiring` a firing case for that branch (mutate the dispatch-branch `echo` and assert), since the current pin passes on the string's presence anywhere in the job. A governed text stating behaviour the tree does not deliver is PD10's "declared ≠ enforced"; FAIL until fixed.

**Should-fix**

2. **The preflight runs this PR's new modes from the SELECTED commit's tree.** The select step detaches to the chosen commit before `Setup workspace`, and every later step runs `node scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs …` from that tree. Until the newest commit with the full battery green ON it is at or after this PR's merge, that tree's `snapshot-next.mjs` has no `stable-lane` mode (prints usage, exit 1, writes no `refusal`) and its `preflight`/`dry-run` ignore `--quiet-skip` and `--commit` — so the first daily run(s) go red with `refusal == ''` and the card files a false "unexpected refusal". Transient (clears with the first green nightly after the merge) and inherited from the lane's design (the 2026-09-29 amendment's "Known edges" names the same split), but it is the first thing the maintainer will see from the lane. Either run the lane's own tooling from the workflow's commit (take the scripts from `GITHUB_SHA` before the detach, or run `stable-lane` before it), or state the edge in the lane header and the ADR and accept one card.
3. **ADR line 293 claims to replace a reading the record never carried.** "The quiet skip replaces this record's earlier reading of a scheduled refusal as a red run" — the merged 2026-11-05 amendment is dispatch-only and has no scheduled-refusal reading; the red-run reading was this PR's own first draft (dev report 6679395057) and the card's acceptance line. Reword to what it replaces (the card's acceptance criterion / the draft), or drop the sentence.
4. **ADR "Trial readings for the #29466 report" defines the director's report metrics**, which is neither of the four bound lines nor one of the five confirmed details. The section is useful and non-normative in intent; mark it as this record's reading, not the ruling's (the house phrase the 2026-11-05 amendment uses), so it is not read later as a decision the maintainer confirmed.
5. **`dryRun()`'s early returns write no `reason` output.** A dirty tree or a missing `node_modules/.bin/changeset` returns exit 3 without `writeStepOutputs`, so the card's reason line reads "no reason was recorded by the run". Record the reason as the catch path does.

### ② Semver level

None. The diff touches `.github/workflows/**`, `docs/**` and `scripts/**` only; no published package moves, so `skip-changeset` is correct and `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier H: `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `docs/adr/0125-*.md` are Tier H register rows (one path makes the whole PR Tier H); PR is a draft on the base repository (not a fork), no reviewers, no assignees. Lands only by the maintainer's hand or an authorized approval; this record is the complete review the card and the 2026-10-25 rule require, not a landing record.
- PR body: `Fixes #30832`, `Ruling-ref: 6677910954`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` present; labels `documentation`, `ci/cd`, `size/xl`, `skip-changeset`. The body matches the tree except for the sentence must-fix 1 falsifies ("the same reading on a dispatch exits 1 with the same outputs") — judged on the tree.
- Check-runs on `5fe2149385`: all completed; every gate-carrying required context is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`); `Build Core` is `skipped` by ci.yml's filter contract (`needs.filter.outputs.core != 'false'`) on a diff with no core path — a skipped required context, not a red one. `Check Changeset` skipped by the label. Nothing in progress.
- The card job's "no card on a dispatch's expected refusal" and the publish-failure body's version line both rely on a FAILED upstream job's `outputs` being readable by an `always()` dependant (`needs.snapshot-next-preflight.outputs.refusal`, `needs.snapshot-next.outputs.version`). GitHub documents job outputs as available to downstream jobs; nothing in this repo has measured it on a failed job. The failure mode would be one false card on a human dispatch (the step re-judges on the same env), never a publish. Measure on the first dispatch refusal and record it in platform-readings.
- `docs/releases-maintenance.md` is edited beyond detail 5's "只加一段 ADR-0125 增补": the release-channels row and the two-crons sentence. The row is the consumer table the 2026-11-05 amendment itself names as the lane's consumer and the card's acceptance requires; it states no rule. Noted, not a fix.
- `stale-prompts` still runs on a snapshot DISPATCH (its `if:` excludes `refresh_version_pr` only) — unchanged from main, and the ruling leaves the sweep untouched; it never runs on either cron.
- The merge commits `a4bb83b2a4` and `5fe2149385` carry git's default message without the `Claude-Session` / `Co-authored-by` trailer pair (disclosed in dev report 6685251006); the landing's merge method decides whether they survive.
- Edge, stated not flagged: a prompt approved minutes before the 01:17Z tick is `in_progress` and untouched by the supersede; today's `snapshot-next` then pends behind it in the group and, once approved, its post-approval preflight refuses `same-commit` loudly if the candidate is the same commit, filing the card as a publish failure with "nothing reached npm". Rare on a `main` that moves daily, and loud rather than silent.

### ④ Design judgment

- `release.yml` against ruling 6677910954 and the five details: the mechanism is right — one `schedule:` with two crons told apart by `github.event.schedule`, every scheduled job naming its own, every stable job unreachable from either cron, the snapshot job held whole at `environment: release`, and a supersede that is a judged cancel of exactly one shape rather than `cancel-in-progress`. The verdict plumbing (`refusal`/`reason` as job outputs, `||` chains in step order, `refusal == ''` as the queue/cancel/card gate) is the simplest shape that lets a green run mean "nothing to propose" without `continue-on-error`. The one defect is the shell branch in must-fix 1, which is the only refusing path not routed through `proposalVerdict`; routing the select step's verdict through the script (a `--quiet-skip`-aware `select` mode) would remove the duplicated classification.
- ADR-0125's 2026-11-06 amendment against its first consumer (`release.yml`) and the ruling: it restates the four bound lines as sentences, names the three replaced sentences with dated pointers in the shape the 2026-09-29 and 2026-11-05 amendments set, keeps D1–D6 and both earlier amendments intact, and states the five details as confirmed. Two sentences overreach (should-fix 3 and 4). Against its consumer it is accurate except where must-fix 1 makes the tree fall short of line 293–294.
- `snapshot-next.mjs`: `proposalVerdict` is the right single meeting point of kinds, flag and exit code; `SNAPSHOT_EXPECTED_REFUSALS` spelled once in the card's module and imported here keeps the two readers agreeing; `stable-lane` reusing the stable sweep's readers (not re-reading the API its own way) is the correct ownership call. `judgeSnapshotPrompts` refuses in the safe order (stable prompt, event, status, job, environment, age).
- `scheduled-full-run{,-card}.mjs`: extending the existing filer with a second identity and step instead of a second filer honours "one route, one owner"; `withBlockNote` taking the identity's footer is the minimal change to keep the block note above the right footer.
- `validate.mjs`: a cron-aware `jobsStartedBy` that answers UNKNOWN when the cron is not named is the honest reading; the pins read the crons off the file rather than spelling them, so the hour can move in one place.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30832-snapshot-daily-schedule`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e4c7785c5aa732d361ccb580635af7d0ae603087`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md, .github/workflows/release.yml + scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs (delta); scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run-card.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs, docs/releases-maintenance.md (unchanged since round 1); scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs, scripts/release-github-releases.mjs, scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs, scripts/release-snapshot-publish.sh, AGENTS.md Prime Directive 15 (main, untouched)

Delta review of the round-1 FAIL record (comment 6685551244 on #30832). Read against: `git diff 5fe2149385..e4c7785c5a` with the branch fetched read-only into `refs/review/pr-30862-r2`; the dev's delta report 6686655794 and the live PR body, read as claims and checked in the tree; the round-1 record's five findings. Not inputs to the verdict: the dev's or the seat's conclusions.

**Separating the merges from the dev's commits.** The range holds four commits: `a15e462dd6` (ci), `04d2ff1b6d` (adr) and two merges of `origin/main`, `943fc6da72` and `e4c7785c5a`. Between the two merge bases (`26c965cb8f` to `616311c126`) main touched none of the seven files in the PR, nor AGENTS.md, release-pending-publish.mjs or release-snapshot-publish.sh; the two dev commits account for every changed line in release.yml, ADR-0125 and snapshot-next.mjs (the dev-only diff and the whole-range diff of those three files are line-identical). The net diff against main is still the same seven files (+2622/-196). Nothing else moved.

### ① Derived judgments

**M1 (must-fix 1) — closed.** release.yml's select step now writes `refusal=no-green-commit` on the dispatch branch as well: after `fi`, `echo "refusal=no-green-commit"`, `echo "reason=..."`, an `::error::` naming the kind as "an expected refusal, loud on a dispatch; no card", `exit 1`. With `refusal` non-empty the card job's first case (`result == 'failure' && outputs.refusal == ''`) is false and `snapshotCardCase` judges the same inputs the same way, so a maintainer dispatching while main has no green commit gets a red run and no p1 card — the behaviour the ADR, the lane header and the PR body state. The pin now fires on that branch specifically: `snapshotWiring` locates the branch by anchors (the `jq -e '.ok == false and .commit == null'` line, then `if [ "${EVENT_NAME}" = 'schedule' ]; then`, then `fi`, then `exit 1`), slices the if-to-fi text as the schedule branch and the fi-to-exit text as the dispatch branch, and requires the `refusal=no-green-commit` echo in each, with distinct findings ("on the SCHEDULE branch" / "on the DISPATCH branch"). The battery "the quiet skip and the card" (16 to 20 cases) adds: both present and silent; removing the dispatch echo alone (regex anchored on the 14-space `fi` line) fires the dispatch pin and not the schedule one; removing the 16-space schedule echo alone fires the schedule pin; replacing the `schedule` test with `if false` fires "does not classify". I confirmed each mutation regex matches the head text (indentation and spelling). The round-1 pin gap (presence anywhere in the job) is gone.

**S2 (should-fix 2) — closed; sound and complete.**

- Mechanism: both `snapshot-next-preflight` and `snapshot-next` carry job env `SNAPSHOT_NEXT_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}` and one step "Take the lane's tooling from the workflow's own commit": `mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lane-tooling"`, `git archive --format=tar "${GITHUB_SHA}" scripts | tar -x -C ...`, `ln -s "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/node_modules" .../lane-tooling/node_modules`. In the preflight it sits after Setup Node.js and before the select step's `git checkout --quiet --detach`; in the snapshot job after the checkout of the selected commit (`fetch-depth: 0`, so `GITHUB_SHA` — main's tip at trigger — is fetched) and before `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-workspace`. `laneRoot(env)` returns `resolve(env.SNAPSHOT_NEXT_ROOT)` when set, else the file's own `../..`; `REPO_ROOT = laneRoot()`.
- Completeness: all seven `snapshot-next.mjs` calls in the two jobs are `node "${RUNNER_TEMP}/lane-tooling/scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs" MODE` — preflight job: `stable-lane`, `preflight --commit`, `dry-run`; snapshot job: `preflight --commit --record`, `record-commit`, `guard --pack-dir --commit`, `verify`. Zero `node scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs` lines remain in either job (`OFF_TREE_CALL` pin, plus pins for exactly one take per job, the take before the detach / before the install, the link line, the env line at job indent, and no call before the take — battery "the lane's tooling runs from the workflow's own commit", 6 cases). The supersede job's `node scripts/ci/snapshot-next.mjs supersede --workflow release.yml` runs from main's own checkout at `github.sha` with no detach, so it is the workflow commit's script already; the card job imports `scheduled-full-run-card.mjs` from the same checkout. The select step's `scheduled-full-run.mjs --snapshot-commit` and `--release-gate` run before the detach, from the workflow commit. No path remains where the selected tree's old script runs the lane's checks.
- Every CLI mode reads the tree through `REPO_ROOT`: `preflight` (`readOptional(join(root, PRE_JSON))`, `readPreJsonAt(root, mainRef)`, `listWorkspacePackages(root)`), `record-commit` (`workspaceState(root)`), `guard` (`changesetBin(root)`, `run(..., { cwd: root })`), `dry-run` (`treeState/restoreTree(root)`, `changesetBin(root)`), `stable-lane` (`versionCommitsOf({ cwd: root })` plus the Actions API). `--workflow release.yml` is an Actions API workflow id, not a file path. The two paths resolved against the copy's own directory (`RELEASE_WORKFLOW`, `PUBLISH_SCRIPT`) are read in `--self-test` only, which the lane never runs. `release-github-releases.mjs`'s own `REPO_ROOT` is the default of `listWorkspacePackages(root = REPO_ROOT)` and snapshot-next passes `root` at both call sites; `cli-build-prerequisite.mjs`'s `atRepoRoot` is not on the lane's path. Verified usage text: "SNAPSHOT_NEXT_ROOT=DIR names the tree every mode reads, when this file does not sit in it".
